chapters.title: Be Strong and Courageous
chapters.html:
Joshua 1

The LORD Speaks to Joshua

1And it came to pass after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD that the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant,

2"Moses My servant is dead. And now get up, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the sons of Israel.

3Every place on which the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, as I promised Moses.

4From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, to the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun, will be your border.

5No one will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not let you go or forsake you.

6Be strong and courageous, for you will cause this people to inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.

7Only be strong and very courageous, to be careful to do according to all the instruction that Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.

8This book of the instruction shall not depart from your mouth. You shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do according to all that is written in it, for then you will make your way succeed, and then you will prosper.

9Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not tremble and do not lose heart, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."

Three Days

10Then Joshua commanded the officials of the people, saying,

11"Pass through the camp and command the people, saying, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three days you are crossing this Jordan to go in and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"

12To the Reubenites, to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,

13"Remember the word that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, saying, 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and will give you this land.'

14Your wives, your little ones and your livestock shall stay in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan, but you shall cross over in ranks before your brothers, all the mighty men of valor, and help them,

15until the LORD gives your brothers rest as He has given you, and they too possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and possess it, the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise."

16They answered Joshua, saying, "All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.

17Just as we listened to Moses in all things, so we will listen to you. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as He was with Moses.

18Anyone who rebels against your command and does not listen to your words in all that you command him shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous."

Notes

  • v1 "after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD" — the book opens where Deuteronomy ends (Deuteronomy 34:5, Moses the servant of the LORD died there). Joshua is Moses' attendant, meshart Moshe, the young man of Exodus 33:11 who would not move out of the tent.

  • v2 "Moses My servant is dead. And now get up" — no time is given to grief beyond the thirty days of Deuteronomy 34:8. The promise now passes to the one who is left.

  • vv3–5 — God repeats to Joshua the words of Deuteronomy 11:24–25, Every place on which the sole of your foot treads, and of Deuteronomy 31:6, He will not let you go or forsake you, now in the first person: I will not let you go.

  • vv6, 7, 9, 18 "Be strong and courageous" — chazaq ve-emats, four times in the chapter, as Moses said it to Joshua in Deuteronomy 31:7 and 23. The last time it is the people who say it to him.

  • v7 "all the instruction that Moses My servant commanded you" — the courage asked of Joshua is not first for battle but for keeping the instruction, to the right or to the left (Deuteronomy 17:11, 20).

  • v8 "meditate on it day and night" — ve-hagita bo, murmur it, the verb of reading aloud under the breath. Psalm 1:2 says the same of the happy man: on His instruction he meditates day and night.

  • v11 "in three days" — the crossing will come in 3:2, at the end of three days, after the spies of chapter 2 return.

  • vv12–15 the two and a half tribes — the agreement of Numbers 32:16–18, we ourselves will arm and go quickly before the sons of Israel, now called in. In ranks, chamushim, the word of Exodus 13:18, where the sons of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt in ranks.

  • v18 "Only be strong and courageous" — the people give Joshua back the words God gave him.

chapters.title: Rahab and the Spies
chapters.html:
Joshua 2

Rahab Hides the Spies

1Joshua son of Nun sent two men secretly from Shittim as spies, saying, "Go, look over the land, and Jericho." They went and entered the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and they lay down there.

2It was told to the king of Jericho, "Men of the sons of Israel have come here tonight to search out the land."

3The king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who entered your house, for they have come to search out all the land."

4But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.

5When the gate was about to be shut at dark, the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them."

6But she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.

7The men pursued them on the road to the Jordan, as far as the fords, and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out after them.

The Oath on the Roof

8Before the men lay down, she came up to them on the roof

9and said to the men, "I know that the LORD has given you the land, and that terror of you has fallen on us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt before you.

10For we have heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you destroyed completely.

11We heard, and our hearts melted, and no spirit remained in anyone because of you, for the LORD your God — He is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.

12And now, please swear to me by the LORD, since I have shown you loyal love, that you also will show loyal love to my father's house, and give me a true sign,

13that you will let my father and my mother, my brothers and my sisters, and all who belong to them live, and deliver our lives from death."

14The men said to her, "Our life for yours, to die — if you do not tell this business of ours. And it shall come to pass, when the LORD gives us the land, that we will deal with you in loyal love and truth."

15Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was in the wall of the city, and she lived in the wall.

16She said to them, "Go to the hill country, so that the pursuers do not come upon you. Hide there three days until the pursuers return, and afterward go your way."

17The men said to her, "We will be free of this oath of yours that you have made us swear,

18unless, when we enter the land, you tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and gather your father and your mother, your brothers and all your father's house to you into the house.

19And it shall come to pass that anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be free. But anyone who is with you in the house, his blood will be on our head if a hand is laid on him.

20If you tell this business of ours, we will be free of your oath that you have made us swear."

21She said, "According to your words, so be it." She sent them away, and they went, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

The Spies Return

22They went and came to the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers searched all along the road and did not find them.

23Then the two men came back down from the hill country, crossed over, and came to Joshua son of Nun and told him all that had happened to them.

24They said to Joshua, "Truly the LORD has given all the land into our hands, and all the inhabitants of the land melt before us."

Notes

  • v1 "two men… as spies" — forty years earlier Moses sent twelve, and ten brought back fear (Numbers 13–14). Joshua, one of the two who did not, sends two, secretly.

  • v1 "a prostitute whose name was Rahab" — ishah zonah. Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 both call her Rahab the prostitute, and both praise her. Matthew 1:5 puts her in the line of David: Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab.

  • v6 "stalks of flax" — pishtei ha-ets, flax of the tree: the long stalks, laid out on the flat roof to dry before their fibers were beaten out for linen.

  • v9 "terror of you has fallen on us… all the inhabitants of the land melt" — the Song of the Sea, Exodus 15:15–16: All who live in Canaan melted in fear. Terror and dread fell on them. Rahab reports that the song has come true.

  • v11 "He is God in the heavens above and on the earth below" — the confession of Deuteronomy 4:39, the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below, spoken by a Canaanite woman.

  • vv12, 14 "loyal love" — chesed, the covenant word. She asks for it, and the men promise chesed ve-emet, loyal love and truth, the pair of God's own name in Exodus 34:6, abundant in loyal love and truth.

  • v18 "this cord of scarlet thread" — tiqvat chut ha-shani. Tiqvah means cord here and in v21; elsewhere it is the ordinary word for hope. The scarlet in the window marks the house to be spared, as the blood on the doorposts did (Exodus 12:13).

  • v19 "his blood will be on his own head" — the house is a place of safety only for those inside it, as on the night of the Passover no one was to go out from the doorway of his house until morning (Exodus 12:22).

  • v24 "Truly the LORD has given all the land into our hands" — the report the spies of Numbers 13 did not bring.

chapters.title: Crossing the Jordan
chapters.html:
Joshua 3

Follow the Ark

1Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the sons of Israel, and they spent the night there before they crossed.

2And it came to pass at the end of three days that the officials passed through the camp

3and commanded the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the Levitical priests carrying it, then you shall set out from your place and go after it.

4But there shall be a distance between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not passed this way before."

5Joshua said to the people, "Make yourselves holy, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."

6Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and cross over before the people." They took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people.

The Waters Will Stand

7The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.

8As for you, command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, saying, 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand still in the Jordan.'"

9Joshua said to the sons of Israel, "Come here and hear the words of the LORD your God."

10Joshua said, "By this you will know that the living God is among you, and that He will surely drive out before you the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Hivite and the Perizzite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Jebusite.

11The ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing over before you into the Jordan.

12Now take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

13And it shall come to pass, when the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, the waters coming down from above, and they will stand as a single wall."

The People Cross on Dry Ground

14When the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant before the people,

15and when those carrying the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests carrying the ark dipped into the edge of the water — the Jordan overflows all its banks all the days of harvest —

16the waters coming down from above stood still. They rose up as a single wall, very far away, from Adam, the city beside Zarethan, and those going down to the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. The people crossed opposite Jericho.

17The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel was crossing on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.

Notes

  • v4 "about two thousand cubits" — roughly half a mile. The ark leads, and the people keep far enough back to see it: so that you may know the way you are to go, for you have not passed this way before, mi-temol shilshom, the phrase of Deuteronomy 19:4.

  • v5 "Make yourselves holy" — hitqaddeshu, as the people were made holy before Sinai in Exodus 19:10.

  • v7 "as I was with Moses, so I will be with you" — the promise of 1:5, now to be seen by all Israel. The crossing is Joshua's Sea of Reeds.

  • v10 "the living God" — el chai, a title rare in the Torah; Deuteronomy 5:26 has the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire.

  • vv11, 13 "the Lord of all the earth" — adon kol ha-arets. The ark that goes into the river belongs to the Lord of the whole earth, not a local god of Israel.

  • vv13, 16 "a single wall" — ned echad, the word of the Song of the Sea, Exodus 15:8, The flowing waters stood like a wall.

  • v15 "the Jordan overflows all its banks all the days of harvest" — the crossing comes at the spring flood, when the river is at its widest (4:19, the first month).

  • v16 "from Adam, the city beside Zarethan" — the waters stop far upstream, so the riverbed runs dry for miles. The written text has be-Adam, at Adam; the reading tradition, followed here, has me-Adam, from Adam: the pile-up reached from Adam down. See the map after Joshua 24, stage 15.

  • v17 "on dry ground" — be-charavah, the word of Exodus 14:21, where the LORD made the sea into dry ground.

chapters.title: Twelve Stones
chapters.html:
Joshua 4

Stones from the Riverbed

1And it came to pass, when the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, that the LORD said to Joshua,

2"Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe,

3and command them, saying, 'Take up for yourselves twelve stones from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm, and carry them over with you and set them down in the lodging place where you spend the night.'"

4Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the sons of Israel, one man from each tribe.

5Joshua said to them, "Cross over before the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you lift a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel,

6so that this may be a sign among you. When your sons ask tomorrow, saying, 'What are these stones to you?'

7you shall say to them, 'The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off.' These stones shall be a memorial for the sons of Israel forever."

8The sons of Israel did so, as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the LORD had told Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel, and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.

9Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood, and they are there to this day.

The Ark Comes Up

10The priests carrying the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was finished that the LORD commanded Joshua to tell the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua. The people hurried and crossed over.

11When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over before the people.

12The sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over in ranks before the sons of Israel, as Moses had told them.

13About forty thousand armed for war crossed over before the LORD to battle, to the plains of Jericho.

14On that day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him as they had feared Moses, all the days of his life.

15The LORD said to Joshua,

16"Command the priests who carry the ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."

17Joshua commanded the priests, saying, "Come up out of the Jordan."

18When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up onto dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.

The Stones at Gilgal

19The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped at Gilgal on the east edge of Jericho.

20Those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.

21He said to the sons of Israel, "When your sons ask their fathers tomorrow, saying, 'What are these stones?'

22you shall let your sons know, saying, 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry land.'

23For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed, as the LORD your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which He dried up before us until we had crossed,

24so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of the LORD, that it is strong, so that you may fear the LORD your God all the days."

Notes

  • vv3, 9 two sets of twelve stones — one set carried to the camp at Gilgal (v20), the other set up in the riverbed where the priests stood (v9), there to this day: one visible to all, one under the water.

  • vv6–7, 21–22 "When your sons ask tomorrow" — the question of the Passover (Exodus 13:14, when your son asks you tomorrow, 'What is this?') and of the commandments (Deuteronomy 6:20). The answer is again a story: Israel crossed this Jordan on dry land.

  • v12 "in ranks" — chamushim, as in 1:14 and Exodus 13:18; the two and a half tribes keep their promise to Moses (Numbers 32).

  • v14 "they feared him as they had feared Moses" — the promise of 3:7 kept: Today I will begin to make you great.

  • v16 "the ark of the Testimony" — the name used in Exodus for the ark holding the tablets of the Testimony. Elsewhere in these chapters it is the ark of the covenant.

  • v19 "the tenth day of the first month" — the day the Passover lamb was chosen in Egypt (Exodus 12:3, On the tenth of this month). Forty years later to the season, Israel enters the land, and keeps Passover four days later (5:10).

  • v19 "Gilgal" — from galal, to roll; 5:9 gives the name its meaning.

  • v23 "as the LORD your God did to the Sea of Reeds" — the Jordan is the second sea. The first crossing ended the slavery; the second begins the inheritance.

  • v24 "so that all the peoples of the earth may know" — Rahab had already heard (2:10). The sign is for the nations as well as for Israel's sons.

About forty thousand armed for war crossed over before the LORD to battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him as they had feared Moses, all the days of his life.
The LORD said to Joshua,
"Command the priests who carry the ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
Joshua commanded the priests, saying, "Come up out of the Jordan."

When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up onto dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.
The Stones at Gilgal
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped at Gilgal on the east edge of Jericho.
Those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.
He said to the sons of Israel, "When your sons ask their fathers tomorrow, saying, 'What are these stones?'
you shall let your sons know, saying, 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry land.'
For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed, as the LORD your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which He dried up before us until we had crossed,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of the LORD, that it is strong, so that you may fear the LORD your God all the days."

chapters.title: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
chapters.html:
Joshua 5

The Second Circumcision

1And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the west and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the sons of Israel until they had crossed, that their hearts melted, and there was no longer any spirit in them because of the sons of Israel.

2At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make for yourself flint knives, and circumcise the sons of Israel again, a second time."

3So Joshua made himself flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.

4This is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they came out of Egypt.

5All the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people born in the wilderness on the way after they came out of Egypt had not been circumcised.

6For the sons of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness until the whole nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, were gone, because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD. The LORD swore to them that He would not let them see the land that the LORD had sworn to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

7Their sons, whom He raised up in their place, these Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.

8When the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they stayed in their places in the camp until they were healed.

9The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you." So the name of that place is called Gilgal to this day.

The First Passover in the Land

10The sons of Israel camped at Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.

11They ate of the produce of the land on the day after the Passover, unleavened bread and roasted grain, on that very day.

12The manna ceased on the day after, when they ate of the produce of the land, and there was no more manna for the sons of Israel. They ate of the yield of the land of Canaan that year.

The Commander of the LORD's Army

13When Joshua was by Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and a man was standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"

14He said, "No — I am the commander of the army of the LORD. Now I have come." Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and said to him, "What does my lord say to his servant?"

15The commander of the LORD's army said to Joshua, "Take your sandal off your foot, for the place on which you are standing is holy." Joshua did so.

Notes

  • v1 "their hearts melted" — the words of Rahab in 2:11, our hearts melted, now said of all the kings west of the Jordan.

  • vv2–3 "flint knives" — charvot tsurim, swords of flint. Zipporah took a flint to circumcise her son in Exodus 4:25.

  • vv4–7 — the generation that left Egypt had been circumcised; the one born in the wilderness had not. The oath of v6 is the oath of Numbers 14:28–33, Your sons shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years.

  • v6 "to give us" — the narrator slips into the first person, speaking as one of the generation that entered.

  • v9 "I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt" — galloti, from galal, to roll, and so Gilgal. What the disgrace of Egypt was is not said: perhaps the reproach of the uncircumcised, perhaps the taunt that God brought Israel out only to kill them in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 9:28).

  • v10 "the fourteenth day of the month" — the date of Exodus 12:6. The first Passover was kept in Egypt, and the Torah records one more, at Sinai (Numbers 9:5). The next the text records is this one, the first in the land.

  • v11 "unleavened bread and roasted grain" — matsot ve-qalui: the first food grown in Canaan. Leviticus 23:14 forbade eating roasted grain from the new harvest until the offering was brought.

  • v12 "The manna ceased" — Exodus 16:35: They ate the manna until they came to the edge of the land of Canaan. The bread from heaven stops on the day the bread of the land begins.

  • vv13–15 "the commander of the army of the LORD" — sar tseva YHWH. Joshua asks which side he is on, and the answer is No: he is not on Joshua's side; Joshua is on his. Now I have come: the sentence seems to break off.

  • v15 "Take your sandal off your foot" — the words at the burning bush, Exodus 3:5, Take your sandals off your feet, for the place you are standing on is holy ground. Joshua's call repeats Moses'.

chapters.title: The Walls of Jericho
chapters.html:
Joshua 6

Seven Days Around the City

1Jericho was shut up tight because of the sons of Israel; no one went out and no one came in.

2The LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and its mighty men of valor.

3You shall march around the city, all the men of war, going around the city once. So you shall do for six days.

4Seven priests shall carry seven rams' horns before the ark. On the seventh day you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horns.

5And it shall come to pass, when they make a long blast with the ram's horn, when you hear the sound of the horn, that all the people shall give a great shout, and the wall of the city will fall down in its place, and the people shall go up, each man straight ahead."

6So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven rams' horns before the ark of the LORD."

7He said to the people, "Go forward and march around the city, and let the armed men go on before the ark of the LORD."

8When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns before the LORD went forward and blew the horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.

9The armed men went before the priests who blew the horns, and the rear guard went after the ark, with the horns blowing all the while.

10But Joshua commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout or let your voice be heard, and no word shall go out of your mouth until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."

11So he had the ark of the LORD go around the city, circling it once, and they went into the camp and spent the night in the camp.

12Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

13The seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns before the ark of the LORD went on, blowing the horns as they went, and the armed men went before them, and the rear guard went after the ark of the LORD, with the horns blowing all the while.

14They marched around the city once on the second day and returned to the camp. So they did for six days.

The Seventh Day

15And it came to pass on the seventh day that they rose early at the dawning of the day and marched around the city in the same manner seven times. Only on that day did they march around the city seven times.

16The seventh time, when the priests blew the horns, Joshua said to the people, "Shout, for the LORD has given you the city!

17The city and all that is in it shall be devoted to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.

18But as for you, keep away from what is devoted to the LORD, so that you do not devote it and then take some of it, and make the camp of Israel doomed and bring trouble on it.

19All silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD; they shall go into the treasury of the LORD."

20So the people shouted, and the horns were blown. When the people heard the sound of the horn, the people gave a great shout, and the wall fell down in its place, and the people went up into the city, each man straight ahead, and they took the city.

21They destroyed everything in the city, man and woman, young and old, ox and sheep and donkey, with the sword.

Rahab Saved

22To the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the prostitute's house, and bring out the woman and all who belong to her from there, as you swore to her."

23The young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and her mother, her brothers and all who belonged to her. They brought out all her family and put them outside the camp of Israel.

24They burned the city with fire, and all that was in it. Only the silver and the gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

25But Rahab the prostitute, her father's household and all who belonged to her, Joshua let live, and she has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

26Joshua made them swear an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before the LORD is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates."

27The LORD was with Joshua, and his fame was in all the land.

Notes

  • v1 "shut up tight" — sogeret u-mesuggeret, the verb twice, closed and closed up. The city that let the spies out through a window (2:15) now opens nothing.

  • vv4–16 sevens — seven priests, seven horns, seven days, seven circuits on the seventh day. The conquest begins as a liturgy.

  • v4 "rams' horns" — shofrot ha-yovelim. Yovel, ram's horn, is the horn of Exodus 19:13, When the ram's horn sounds long, they may come up the mountain, and it gives its name to the year of jubilee (Leviticus 25).

  • v5 "a long blast" — bi-meshokh, the verb of Exodus 19:13, sounds long.

  • v10 "You shall not shout" — six days of silence, and then one shout.

  • v17 "devoted to the LORD" — cherem: the city is given entire to God, as Deuteronomy 20:16–17 commanded for the cities of the land. Rahab the prostitute shall live — the one exception, by oath (2:14).

  • v18 "bring trouble on it" — va-akhartem, the verb that will give the valley of Achor its name after Achan does exactly this (7:25–26).

  • v20 "the wall fell down in its place" — tachteiha, under itself. Hebrews 11:30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after they had been encircled for seven days.

  • v23 "outside the camp of Israel" — at first. By v25 she has lived among Israel to this day.

  • v26 the curse on Jericho — 1 Kings 16:34 records its fulfillment: In his days Hiel of Bethel built Jericho. With Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and with Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke through Joshua son of Nun.

chapters.title: Achan and the Valley of Achor
chapters.html:
Joshua 7

Defeat at Ai

1But the sons of Israel broke faith over what was devoted to the LORD. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted, and the anger of the LORD burned against the sons of Israel.

2Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." The men went up and spied out Ai.

3They returned to Joshua and said to him, "Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for they are few."

4So about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.

5The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them and chased them from before the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down on the descent. The hearts of the people melted and became like water.

6Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.

7Joshua said, "Ah, Lord GOD, why did You ever bring this people across the Jordan, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay beyond the Jordan!

8Please, Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?

9The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and surround us and cut off our name from the earth. What will You do for Your great name?"

Israel Has Sinned

10The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up. Why are you lying on your face?

11Israel has sinned. They have also transgressed My covenant that I commanded them. They have also taken some of what was devoted; they have also stolen, and also lied, and also put it among their own belongings.

12That is why the sons of Israel cannot stand before their enemies; they turn their backs before their enemies, because they themselves are now doomed. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy what is devoted from among you.

13Get up, make the people holy, and say, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is something devoted among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove what is devoted from among you.'

14In the morning you shall come near by your tribes. And it shall come to pass that the tribe that the LORD takes shall come near by clans, and the clan that the LORD takes shall come near by households, and the household that the LORD takes shall come near man by man.

15And it shall come to pass that the one who is taken with what is devoted shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and because he has done an outrage in Israel."

Achan Is Taken

16Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.

17He brought near the clans of Judah, and he took the clan of the Zerahites. He brought near the clan of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.

18He brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

19Joshua said to Achan, "My son, please give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give Him praise. Tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me."

20Achan answered Joshua and said, "Truly, I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This and this is what I did:

21I saw among the spoil a beautiful cloak from Shinar, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, and I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."

22Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and it was hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.

23They took them from inside the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the sons of Israel, and they poured them out before the LORD.

24Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver and the cloak and the bar of gold, and his sons and his daughters, his ox and his donkey and his sheep, and his tent and all that he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.

25Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today." All Israel stoned him. They burned them with fire and stoned them.

26They raised over him a great heap of stones, which is there to this day. Then the LORD turned from the heat of His anger. That is why the name of that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.

Notes

  • v1 "the sons of Israel broke faith" — va-yim'alu… ma'al: one man takes, and the text says Israel sinned. God says the same in v11, Israel has sinned, and v12, they themselves are now doomed. The warning of 6:18 has come true: make the camp of Israel doomed.

  • vv3–5 the second spies — this time the report is confident and the attack fails. Thirty-six men fall; the hearts of the people melted, the phrase used of the Canaanites in 2:11 and 5:1, now said of Israel.

  • v7 "Ah, Lord GOD" — ahah Adonai YHWH, a cry of dismay. If only we had been content to stay beyond the Jordan is the complaint of the wilderness generation, now in Joshua's mouth.

  • v9 "What will You do for Your great name?" — the argument Moses used in Deuteronomy 9:28: what will the nations say?

  • v11 "also… also… also" — ve-gam, five times, piling up the charges: sinned, transgressed, taken, stolen, lied, hidden.

  • vv14–18 taken by lot — tribe, clan, household, man. The verb lakhad, take, capture, is the verb of taking a city; now it is used of Israel's own.

  • v19 "give glory to the LORD… and give Him praise" — ten lo todah: confess, and so acknowledge that God has judged rightly.

  • v21 "I saw… I coveted… I took" — va-ere… va-echmedem… va-eqqachem. Chamad is the verb of the Ten Words, You shall not covet (Exodus 20:17). The order is Eve's in Genesis 3:6: she saw, it was desirable, she took.

  • v25 "Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you" — akhartanu… ya'kor'kha, the verb of 6:18, bring trouble on it, and the root of Achor. 1 Chronicles 2:7 even calls him Achar, the troubler of Israel, who broke faith over what was devoted to the LORD. Hosea 2:17 (2:15 in English) turns the name around: the Valley of Achor as a door of hope, tiqvah, the word of Rahab's cord (2:18).

  • v26 "a great heap of stones" — the second heap in the book, after the twelve stones of Gilgal: one to remember a crossing, one to remember a sin.

chapters.title: Ai Taken, and the Altar on Mount Ebal
chapters.html:
Joshua 8

The Ambush

1The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid and do not lose heart. Take all the fighting men with you, and get up, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, and his people, his city and his land.

2You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may take its spoil and its livestock as plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush against the city behind it."

3So Joshua and all the fighting men got up to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty men of valor and sent them out by night.

4He commanded them, saying, "See, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, and all of you be ready.

5I and all the people who are with me will approach the city. And it shall come to pass, when they come out against us as at the first, that we will flee before them.

6They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as at the first.' So we will flee before them,

7and you shall rise up from the ambush and seize the city, and the LORD your God will give it into your hand.

8And it shall come to pass, when you have taken the city, that you shall set the city on fire. You shall do according to the word of the LORD. See, I have commanded you."

9So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. Joshua spent that night among the people.

10Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.

11All the fighting men who were with him went up and drew near and came opposite the city, and camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.

12He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.

13So they stationed the people, the whole camp that was north of the city, and its rear guard west of the city. Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley.

14When the king of Ai saw it, the men of the city hurried and rose early and went out to meet Israel in battle, he and all his people, at the appointed place facing the Arabah. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.

15Joshua and all Israel let themselves be struck before them and fled by the way of the wilderness.

16All the people who were in Ai were called out to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.

17Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.

The Javelin Held Out

18The LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.

19The ambush rose quickly from its place, and they ran as soon as he stretched out his hand, and entered the city and took it, and hurried to set the city on fire.

20The men of Ai turned back and looked, and the smoke of the city was going up to the heavens, and they had no power to flee this way or that. The people who had fled to the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.

21When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that the smoke of the city was going up, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

22The others came out of the city against them, so that they were in the middle of Israel, some on this side and some on that. They struck them down until no survivor or fugitive was left.

23The king of Ai they took alive and brought him to Joshua.

24When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all of them had fallen by the sword until they were finished, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the sword.

25All who fell that day, men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.

26Joshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the javelin until he had destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai completely.

27Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that He commanded Joshua.

28Joshua burned Ai and made it a heap forever, a desolation, to this day.

29The king of Ai he hanged on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua commanded, and they took his body down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.

The Altar on Mount Ebal

30Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

31as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the sons of Israel, as it is written in the book of the instruction of Moses: an altar of whole stones, on which no one had wielded any iron tool. They offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.

32There, on the stones, he wrote a copy of the instruction of Moses, which he had written before the sons of Israel.

33All Israel, with their elders and officials and judges, stood on either side of the ark, opposite the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the guest as well as the native, half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded at the first, to bless the people Israel.

34Afterward he read all the words of the instruction, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the instruction.

35There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women and the little ones and the guests who were going among them.

Notes

  • v1 "Do not be afraid and do not lose heart" — the words of Deuteronomy 1:21 and 31:8, after the defeat of chapter 7.

  • v2 "you may take its spoil and its livestock" — what Achan died for taking at Jericho is given freely at Ai. Had he waited, it would have been his.

  • vv3, 12 thirty thousand… five thousand — two numbers for the ambush. Either there were two ambushes, or the text has kept two accounts side by side; it does not say which.

  • v17 "Ai or Bethel" — Bethel's men are mentioned only here in the battle; the two towns lay close together, as in Genesis 12:8, Bethel on the west and Ai on the east.

  • vv18, 26 "Stretch out the javelin" — kidon, a short spear. Joshua holds it out until the battle is over, as Moses held up his hands against Amalek until the sun went down (Exodus 17:12), with Joshua fighting below.

  • v28 "a heap forever" — tel olam, the words of Deuteronomy 13:16 for a town burned whole to the LORD. Ai, ha-Ai, means the ruin.

  • v29 the king on a tree — taken down at sunset, as Deuteronomy 21:23 commands: his body shall not remain overnight on the tree.

  • vv30–35 the altar on Mount Ebal — the command of Deuteronomy 27:2–8 carried out: an altar of whole stones… You shall not wield any iron tool on them, and the instruction written on stones. The blessing and the curse are read, as Deuteronomy 11:29 and 27:12–13 required.

  • v32 "a copy of the instruction of Moses" — mishneh torat Moshe, the phrase of Deuteronomy 17:18, the king's copy.

  • v35 "the women and the little ones and the guests" — the gathering of Deuteronomy 31:12, the men and the women and the little ones, and your guest. No one is left out of the hearing.

chapters.title: The Gibeonites
chapters.html:
Joshua 9

The Kings Gather

1And it came to pass, when all the kings who were beyond the Jordan heard of it — in the hill country and in the lowland and all along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon, the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite —

2that they gathered together with one mouth to fight against Joshua and against Israel.

The Gibeonites' Trick

3But the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,

4and they too acted with cunning. They went and disguised themselves as envoys, and took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and wineskins worn out and split and tied up,

5and worn-out, patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out clothes on them. All the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbled.

6They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a far country. Now make a covenant with us."

7The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you live among us. How then can we make a covenant with you?"

8They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"

9They said to him, "From a very far country your servants have come, because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard the report of Him, and all that He did in Egypt,

10and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

11Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country said to us, 'Take provisions in your hand for the journey and go to meet them, and say to them, "We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us."'

12This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses as our provision on the day we set out to come to you, and now it is dry and crumbled.

13These wineskins were new when we filled them, and they have split. These clothes of ours and our sandals are worn out from the very long journey."

14The men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask the counsel of the LORD.

15Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore to them.

Found Out

16And it came to pass at the end of three days, after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were their neighbors and were living among them.

17The sons of Israel set out and came to their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.

18The sons of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. All the congregation grumbled against the leaders.

19All the leaders said to all the congregation, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.

20This is what we will do to them: let them live, so that wrath does not come on us because of the oath that we swore to them."

21The leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the leaders had told them.

22Joshua called for them and spoke to them, saying, "Why did you deceive us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you live among us?

23So now you are cursed. There shall never cease to be from among you slaves, cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."

24They answered Joshua and said, "Because it was told, told to your servants that the LORD your God commanded Moses His servant to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you, we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.

25Now we are in your hand. Do to us whatever seems good and right in your eyes."

26He did so to them, and delivered them from the hand of the sons of Israel, and they did not kill them.

27That day Joshua made them cutters of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this day, in the place that He would choose.

Notes

  • v2 "with one mouth" — peh echad, one voice, as all the earth at Babel was one lip (Genesis 11:1). Against them stands one city that chooses otherwise.

  • v4 "acted with cunning" — be-ormah, the root of Genesis 3:1, where the serpent was shrewder than every living thing of the field. They too: as Joshua had used cunning at Ai (8:2, the ambush).

  • vv6, 9 "from a far country" — the law of Deuteronomy 20:10–15 let Israel make peace with cities that are very far from you, not with the nations of the land. The Gibeonites know the law and dress for it.

  • v7 "the Hivites" — Gibeon's people are among the seven nations (3:10), the ones Deuteronomy 7:2 forbade Israel to make a covenant with.

  • v9 "because of the name of the LORD your God" — they say what Rahab said (2:10), we have heard, but leave out what happened at Jericho and Ai, since a far people could not yet know it.

  • v14 "they did not ask the counsel of the LORD" — et pi YHWH, the mouth of the LORD. They tasted the bread and trusted their own judgment.

  • vv18–20 the oath kept — an oath sworn in God's name binds even when it was won by deceit. 2 Samuel 21:1–2 tells how Saul later broke it, and Israel suffered famine for it.

  • v21 "cutters of wood and drawers of water" — the lowest work of the camp, named in Deuteronomy 29:11 for your guest who is inside your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water. The Gibeonites are given the guest's place.

  • v27 "for the altar of the LORD… in the place that He would choose" — the phrase of Deuteronomy 12. The deceivers end up serving at God's altar.

chapters.title: The Day the Sun Stood Still
chapters.html:
Joshua 10

Five Kings Against Gibeon

1And it came to pass, when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and destroyed it completely, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,

2that he was very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.

3So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,

4"Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the sons of Israel."

5The five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon — gathered and went up, they and all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and fought against it.

6The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."

7Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the fighting men with him, and all the mighty men of valor.

8The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will stand before you."

9Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.

10The LORD threw them into panic before Israel, and He dealt them a great defeat at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

11As they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, the LORD threw great stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword.

Sun, Stand Still

12Then Joshua spoke to the LORD on the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the sons of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel:

"Sun, stand still at Gibeon,
and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

13So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped,
until the nation took vengeance on its enemies.

Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the heavens and did not hurry to go down for about a whole day.

14There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.

15Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

The Cave at Makkedah

16These five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.

17It was told to Joshua, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."

18Joshua said, "Roll great stones against the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them.

19But you, do not stay there. Pursue your enemies and cut off their rear guard. Do not let them enter their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."

20When Joshua and the sons of Israel had finished dealing them a very great defeat until they were finished, and the survivors among them had escaped into the fortified cities,

21all the people returned safely to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the sons of Israel.

22Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring these five kings out to me from the cave."

23They did so, and brought these five kings out to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

24When they brought these kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the fighting men who had gone with him, "Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings." They came near and put their feet on their necks.

25Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid and do not lose heart. Be strong and courageous, for so the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."

26Afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees, and they hung on the trees until evening.

27At the time of sunset Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden, and put great stones at the mouth of the cave, which are there to this very day.

The Southern Cities

28Joshua took Makkedah on that day and struck it and its king with the sword. He destroyed them and every person in it completely; he left no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.

29Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

30The LORD gave it also, and its king, into the hand of Israel, and he struck it and every person in it with the sword; he left no survivor in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.

31Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Libnah to Lachish, and camped against it and fought against it.

32The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he took it on the second day and struck it and every person in it with the sword, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

33Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.

34Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Lachish to Eglon, and they camped against it and fought against it.

35They took it on that day and struck it with the sword, and every person in it he destroyed completely on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

36Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

37They took it and struck it with the sword, and its king and all its towns and every person in it; he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. He destroyed it and every person in it completely.

38Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and fought against it.

39He took it, and its king and all its towns, and they struck them with the sword and destroyed every person in it completely; he left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.

40So Joshua struck all the land — the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the slopes — and all their kings. He left no survivor, but destroyed everything that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.

41Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

42All these kings and their land Joshua took at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

43Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

Notes

  • v1 "Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem" — my lord is righteous, a name built like Melchizedek, my king is righteous, the king of Salem who blessed Abram in Genesis 14:18. This is the first time the Bible names the city Jerusalem.

  • v6 "Do not let your hands drop from your servants" — the Gibeonites now call on the covenant that they obtained by deceit, and Joshua honors it.

  • v10 "threw them into panic" — va-yehummem, the verb of the Sea of Reeds, Exodus 14:24, when the LORD threw the camp of Egypt into panic.

  • v11 "great stones… hailstones" — the hail that struck Egypt (Exodus 9) falls now on the Amorites. More die by God's hand than by Israel's.

  • vv12–13 "Sun, stand still" — dom, be silent, be still. Two lines of verse quoted from the Book of Jashar, sefer ha-yashar, the Book of the Upright, a lost collection of songs; 2 Samuel 1:18 quotes it again for David's lament over Saul and Jonathan. The verse gives no account of how; it says what was asked and what happened.

  • v14 "when the LORD listened to the voice of a man" — the wonder the text stresses is not the sun but the hearing: God did what a man asked. The LORD fought for Israel, as Moses promised at the sea: The LORD will fight for you (Exodus 14:14).

  • v15 and v43 — the return to Gilgal is told twice, once in v15 after the poem and again in v43 after the southern campaign. The Greek does not have v15 or v43.

  • v21 "No one sharpened his tongue" — the idiom of Exodus 11:7, not a dog will sharpen its tongue: no one dared say a word.

  • v24 "put your feet on the necks of these kings" — a sign of complete victory, done by the commanders, not by Joshua, so that they would see the promise with their own eyes (v25).

  • vv28–39 six cities — Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, Debir, each told with the same words. The refrain he left no survivor runs through the list.

speech.text: Joshua 10
Five Kings Against Gibeon

And it came to pass, when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and destroyed it completely, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,
that he was very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,
"Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the sons of Israel."

The five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon — gathered and went up, they and all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and fought against it.

The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the fighting men with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will stand before you."
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.
The LORD threw them into panic before Israel, and He dealt them a great defeat at Gibeon, and chased them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, the LORD threw great stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword.
Sun, Stand Still
Then Joshua spoke to the LORD on the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the sons of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the heavens and did not hurry to go down for about a whole day.
There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
The Cave at Makkedah
These five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
It was told to Joshua, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll great stones against the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them.
But you, do not stay there. Pursue your enemies and cut off their rear guard. Do not let them enter their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
When Joshua and the sons of Israel had finished dealing them a very great defeat until they were finished, and the survivors among them had escaped into the fortified cities,
all the people returned safely to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the sons of Israel.
Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring these five kings out to me from the cave."
They did so, and brought these five kings out to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

When they brought these kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the fighting men who had gone with him, "Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings." They came near and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid and do not lose heart. Be strong and courageous, for so the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."
Afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees, and they hung on the trees until evening.

At the time of sunset Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden, and put great stones at the mouth of the cave, which are there to this very day.
The Southern Cities

Joshua took Makkedah on that day and struck it and its king with the sword. He destroyed them and every person in it completely; he left no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

The LORD gave it also, and its king, into the hand of Israel, and he struck it and every person in it with the sword; he left no survivor in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Libnah to Lachish, and camped against it and fought against it.
The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he took it on the second day and struck it and every person in it with the sword, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.
Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Lachish to Eglon, and they camped against it and fought against it.
They took it on that day and struck it with the sword, and every person in it he destroyed completely on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

They took it and struck it with the sword, and its king and all its towns and every person in it; he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. He destroyed it and every person in it completely.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and fought against it.

He took it, and its king and all its towns, and they struck them with the sword and destroyed every person in it completely; he left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua struck all the land — the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the slopes — and all their kings. He left no survivor, but destroyed everything that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
All these kings and their land Joshua took at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

chapters.title: The Northern Kings
chapters.html:
Joshua 11

The Waters of Merom

1And it came to pass, when Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,

2and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, and in the lowland and on the heights of Dor on the west,

3to the Canaanite in the east and the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.

4They went out, they and all their armies with them, a people as many as the sand on the lip of the sea for multitude, with very many horses and chariots.

5All these kings met by appointment, and came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

6The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will give all of them slain before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."

7So Joshua and all the fighting men with him came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and fell upon them.

8The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and eastward as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. They struck them until they had left them no survivor.

9Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.

Hazor Burned

10Joshua turned back at that time and took Hazor, and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor formerly was the head of all these kingdoms.

11They struck every person in it with the sword, destroying them completely. Nothing that breathed was left, and he burned Hazor with fire.

12All the cities of these kings, and all their kings, Joshua took, and struck them with the sword. He destroyed them completely, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.

13But the cities standing on their mounds Israel did not burn, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

14All the spoil of these cities and the livestock the sons of Israel took as plunder for themselves. But every human being they struck with the sword until they had destroyed them; they left nothing that breathed.

15As the LORD had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.

The Whole Land Taken

16So Joshua took all this land: the hill country and all the Negev and all the land of Goshen, and the lowland and the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel and its lowland,

17from the bare mountain that rises toward Seir as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He took all their kings and struck them and put them to death.

18Joshua made war many days with all these kings.

19There was not a city that made peace with the sons of Israel except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They took all of them in battle.

20For it was from the LORD to make their hearts strong to meet Israel in battle, so that they might be destroyed completely and receive no favor, but be wiped out, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

21At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua destroyed them completely, with their cities.

22None of the Anakim was left in the land of the sons of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath and in Ashdod did some remain.

23So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses, and Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.

Notes

  • v1 "Jabin king of Hazor" — a king of the same name and city appears again in Judges 4:2, Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor.

  • v4 "as many as the sand on the lip of the sea" — the image of God's promise to Abraham, Genesis 22:17, as the sand that is on the lip of the sea, here used for Israel's enemies.

  • vv6, 9 "hamstring their horses and burn their chariots" — Israel is not to keep the weapons of the kings. Deuteronomy 17:16 forbade the king to multiply horses.

  • v10 "Hazor… the head of all these kingdoms" — the leading city of the northern alliance; it alone is burned (v13).

  • v13 "standing on their mounds" — al tillam: the tel, the mound of earlier ruins on which a city was rebuilt. The rest were left standing for Israel to live in, as Deuteronomy 6:10 promised: great and good cities that you did not build.

  • v15 "He left nothing undone" — lo hesir davar, he did not remove a word: Joshua did all Moses commanded, as Moses did all God commanded.

  • v18 "many days" — the campaigns of chapters 10–11, told as if at once, took a long time. Caleb's age in 14:7–10 puts it at about seven years.

  • v20 "to make their hearts strong" — le-chazzeq et libbam, the verb of Exodus 4:21, I Myself will make his heart strong. The kings of Canaan are hardened as Pharaoh was.

  • vv21–22 the Anakim — the giants whose size frightened the spies (Numbers 13:33, the sons of Anak). A remnant is left in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod, Philistine cities; Goliath of Gath will come from them (1 Samuel 17:4). See the map after Joshua 24, stage 18.

  • v23 "Then the land had rest from war" — ve-ha-arets shaqetah, the refrain that later closes the stories of the judges (Judges 3:11). The summary looks ahead; 13:1 will say very much of the land remains to be possessed.

chapters.title: The Kings Struck Down
chapters.html:
Joshua 12

Beyond the Jordan

1These are the kings of the land whom the sons of Israel struck down and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

2Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, and half of Gilead, as far as the river Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,

3and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth eastward, and as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, by the way to Beth-jeshimoth, and on the south below the slopes of Pisgah;

4and the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,

5and ruled over Mount Hermon and Salecah and all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

6Moses the servant of the LORD and the sons of Israel struck them down, and Moses the servant of the LORD gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

West of the Jordan

7These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the sons of Israel struck down beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to the bare mountain that rises toward Seir, and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,

8in the hill country and in the lowland, in the Arabah and on the slopes, in the wilderness and in the Negev — the Hittite, the Amorite and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite:

9the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;

10the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

11the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

12the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

13the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

14the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

15the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

16the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

17the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

18the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;

19the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

20the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

21the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

22the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;

23the king of Dor on the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim at Gilgal, one;

24the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings: thirty-one.

Notes

  • vv1–6 the two kings east of the Jordan — Sihon and Og, whose defeat Moses recounted in Deuteronomy 2:26–3:11. The list begins with what Moses did before it tells what Joshua did.

  • v4 "one of the remnant of the Rephaim" — the words of Deuteronomy 3:11, only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim.

  • v6 "Moses the servant of the LORD" — twice in one verse: the conquest east of the Jordan is his, the conquest west is Joshua's (v7).

  • vv9–24 "one… one" — each king is counted like a line in a ledger, echad, one, and the total given at the end: thirty-one.

  • v9 "the king of Jericho… the king of Ai" — the order follows the book: Jericho (chapter 6), Ai (8), the five kings of the south (10), and then the north (11).

  • v14 "Hormah… Arad" — cities of the Negev; Numbers 21:1–3 tells of the king of Arad and the place named Hormah.

  • v20 "Shimron-meron" — the Hebrew has Shimron Meron as one entry; the king of Shimron of 11:1.

  • v23 "the king of Goiim at Gilgal" — Goiim is nations; the name may mean a ruler over mixed peoples. This Gilgal is not Israel's camp by the Jordan.
