chapters.title: The Land That Remains
chapters.html:
Joshua 13

Very Much Land Remains

1Joshua was old, coming on in days, and the LORD said to him, "You are old, coming on in days, and very much of the land remains to be possessed.

2This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites,

3from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north — it is counted as Canaanite — the five lords of the Philistines, the Gazite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite; and the Avvim

4in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;

5and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;

6all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I Myself will drive them out before the sons of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.

7So now divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."

East of the Jordan

8With the other half-tribe of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:

9from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon;

10and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the sons of Ammon;

11and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;

12all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. These Moses struck down and dispossessed.

13But the sons of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.

14Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire of the LORD, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, as He said to it.

Reuben

15Moses gave to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans.

16Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau by Medeba;

17Heshbon and all its cities that are on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,

18Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

19Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,

20Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

21and all the cities of the plateau, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down with the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.

22Balaam son of Beor, the soothsayer, the sons of Israel also killed with the sword among their slain.

23The border of the sons of Reuben was the Jordan and its bank. This is the inheritance of the sons of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

Gad

24Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad according to their clans.

25Their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;

26and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

27and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its bank, as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.

28This is the inheritance of the sons of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.

Half of Manasseh

29Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it was for the half-tribe of the sons of Manasseh according to their clans.

30Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities;

31and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, for the sons of Machir son of Manasseh, for half the sons of Machir according to their clans.

32These are the inheritances that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward.

33But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as He said to them.

Notes

  • v1 "old, coming on in days" — the words said of Abraham in Genesis 24:1, Abraham was old, coming on in days. The conquest summary of 11:23 said Joshua took the whole land; here God says very much of the land remains. Both are true: the land is given, but not yet possessed.

  • v3 "the Shihor, which is east of Egypt" — a branch or channel on Egypt's border. The five lords of the Philistines, seranim, the title the Bible gives only to the Philistine rulers.

  • v6 "I Myself will drive them out… Only allot it" — Joshua is to divide land not yet taken, trusting God to finish what He promised.

  • vv8–33 — a second account of Numbers 32 and Deuteronomy 3:12–17: what Moses gave the two and a half tribes before his death.

  • v13 "Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day" — the first of several notes in Joshua on peoples not driven out. David will marry Maacah, daughter of the king of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:3).

  • vv14, 33 Levi's inheritance — the offerings by fire of the LORD (v14) and the LORD, the God of Israel (v33) are Levi's portion, as promised in Numbers 18:20, I am your share and your inheritance, and Deuteronomy 18:1.

  • v21 "the leaders of Midian" — the same five named in Numbers 31:8, the five kings of Midian. Here they are called princes of Sihon, vassals of the Amorite king.

  • v22 "Balaam son of Beor, the soothsayer" — ha-qosem, the word that Deuteronomy 18:10 forbade in Israel (a soothsayer). His death is told in Numbers 31:8.

  • v30 "Havvoth-jair… sixty cities" — the tent villages Jair took (Numbers 32:41, Deuteronomy 3:14).

in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;

all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I Myself will drive them out before the sons of Israel. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
So now divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
East of the Jordan
With the other half-tribe of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:
from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the sons of Ammon;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. These Moses struck down and dispossessed.
But the sons of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire of the LORD, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, as He said to it.
Reuben
Moses gave to the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau by Medeba;
Heshbon and all its cities that are on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plateau, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down with the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.
Balaam son of Beor, the soothsayer, the sons of Israel also killed with the sword among their slain.
The border of the sons of Reuben was the Jordan and its bank. This is the inheritance of the sons of Reuben according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
Gad
Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad according to their clans.
Their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;
and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its bank, as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.
This is the inheritance of the sons of Gad according to their clans, the cities and their villages.
Half of Manasseh
Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it was for the half-tribe of the sons of Manasseh according to their clans.
Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities;
and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, for the sons of Machir son of Manasseh, for half the sons of Machir according to their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as He said to them.

chapters.title: Caleb's Inheritance
chapters.html:
Joshua 14

Dividing the Land by Lot

1These are the inheritances that the sons of Israel received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the sons of Israel distributed to them.

2Their inheritance was by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

3For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

4For the sons of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to live in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and their possessions.

5As the LORD had commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did, and they divided the land.

Give Me This Hill Country

6The sons of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word that the LORD spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh-barnea.

7I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back word as it was in my heart.

8My brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, but I followed the LORD my God fully.

9Moses swore on that day, saying, 'Surely the land on which your foot has walked shall be an inheritance for you and for your sons forever, because you have followed the LORD my God fully.'

10Now the LORD has kept me alive, as He said, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old.

11I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me. As my strength was then, so my strength is now, for war and for going out and coming in.

12And now give me this hill country of which the LORD spoke on that day, for you heard on that day that the Anakim were there, with great fortified cities. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, as the LORD said."

13Joshua blessed him, and he gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.

14That is why Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, fully.

15The name of Hebron before was Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land had rest from war.

Notes

  • v1 "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses" — the three named in Numbers 34:17–18 for dividing the land. Eleazar comes first; the land is given before the LORD.

  • v2 "by lot" — be-goral, as Numbers 26:55 commanded. The lot leaves the choice to God.

  • v4 "cities to live in, with their pasture lands" — migresheihem, the pasture land around the Levites' towns commanded in Numbers 35:2–5. Chapter 21 lists them.

  • v6 "Caleb… the Kenizzite" — Kenaz is also a name among the clans of Edom (Genesis 36:11). Caleb comes with the sons of Judah, yet carries a clan name found outside Israel, and he is the one held up as having followed the LORD fully.

  • vv7–9 — Caleb tells the story of Numbers 13–14 in his own words. As it was in my heart: his report was honest. The ten made the heart of the people melt, the phrase of 2:11, 5:1 and 7:5.

  • vv8, 9, 14 "followed the LORD… fully" — millé acharei YHWH, three times in the chapter, the words of Numbers 14:24, he has followed Me fully, and Deuteronomy 1:36.

  • v9 "the land on which your foot has walked" — Deuteronomy 1:36: to him and to his sons I will give the land he has walked on.

  • v10 "these forty-five years… eighty-five years old" — forty at Kadesh, thirty-eight years of wandering, and about seven years of conquest since the crossing.

  • v12 "Perhaps the LORD will be with me" — at eighty-five, Caleb asks for the hardest ground in the land: the hill country of the Anakim who frightened the spies.

  • v15 "Kiriath-arba" — town of Arba, the older name of Hebron, as in Genesis 23:2, Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron, where Sarah died.

chapters.title: The Lot of Judah
chapters.html:
Joshua 15

Judah's Borders

1The lot for the tribe of the sons of Judah according to their clans reached to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin at the far south.

2Their south border ran from the end of the Salt Sea, from the tongue of water that faces south,

3and went out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, crossed to Zin, went up south of Kadesh-barnea, crossed to Hezron, went up to Addar and turned around to Karka,

4crossed to Azmon, went out to the Brook of Egypt, and the border ended at the sea. This shall be your south border.

5The east border was the Salt Sea, up to the mouth of the Jordan. The border on the north side ran from the tongue of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.

6The border went up to Beth-hoglah and crossed north of Beth-arabah, and the border went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

7The border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turned north toward Gilgal, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, south of the ravine. The border crossed to the waters of En-shemesh and ended at En-rogel.

8The border went up by the Valley of the Son of Hinnom at the southern slope of the Jebusite — that is, Jerusalem — and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lies west of the Valley of Hinnom, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.

9The border was drawn from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, went out to the cities of Mount Ephron, and was drawn to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim.

10The border turned west from Baalah to Mount Seir, crossed to the northern slope of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon, went down to Beth-shemesh and crossed to Timnah.

11The border went out to the northern slope of Ekron, was drawn to Shikkeron, crossed to Mount Baalah, went out to Jabneel, and the border ended at the sea.

12The west border was the Great Sea and its coast. This is the border of the sons of Judah all around, according to their clans.

Caleb and Achsah

13To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the sons of Judah, at the command of the LORD to Joshua: Kiriath-arba, Arba being the father of Anak, that is, Hebron.

14Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.

15From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir. The name of Debir before was Kiriath-sepher.

16Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give him Achsah my daughter as a wife."

17Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.

18When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"

19She said, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The Cities of Judah

20This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judah according to their clans.

21The cities at the far end of the tribe of the sons of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,

22Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,

23Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,

24Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,

25Hazor-hadattah, Kerioth-hezron, that is, Hazor,

26Amam, Shema, Moladah,

27Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet,

28Hazar-shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,

29Baalah, Iim, Ezem,

30Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,

31Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,

32Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon: in all, twenty-nine cities with their villages.

33In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,

34Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam,

35Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,

36Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen cities with their villages.

37Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad,

38Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel,

39Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,

40Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish,

41Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen cities with their villages.

42Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

43Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,

44Keilah, Achzib and Mareshah: nine cities with their villages.

45Ekron, with its towns and its villages;

46from Ekron to the sea, all that were near Ashdod, with their villages;

47Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea and its coast.

48In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,

49Dannah, Kiriath-sannah, that is, Debir,

50Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

51Goshen, Holon and Giloh: eleven cities with their villages.

52Arab, Dumah, Eshan,

53Janum, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah,

54Humtah, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, and Zior: nine cities with their villages.

55Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

56Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,

57Kain, Gibeah and Timnah: ten cities with their villages.

58Halhul, Beth-zur, Gedor,

59Maarath, Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six cities with their villages.

60Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, and Rabbah: two cities with their villages.

61In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,

62Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi: six cities with their villages.

63But the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the sons of Judah could not drive out, and the Jebusites live with the sons of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

Notes

  • vv1–4 the south border — the line of Numbers 34:3–5, from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom… to the Brook of Egypt, now Judah's own border. Judah's lot comes first, as Judah was first in the march (Numbers 10:14).

  • v6 "the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben" — a landmark, perhaps a standing stone; bohen is thumb. Nothing else is known of Bohan.

  • v7 "the Valley of Achor" — where Achan was stoned (7:26).

  • v8 "the Valley of the Son of Hinnom" — gei ven Hinnom, south of Jerusalem. Gei Hinnom passed into Greek as geenna, the Gehenna of Matthew 5:22, the fire of Gehenna. The city itself is still called the Jebusite here.

  • vv13–19 Caleb, Othniel and Achsah — told again, almost word for word, in Judges 1:10–15. Othniel will be the first of the judges (Judges 3:9).

  • v14 "Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai" — the three descendants of Anak whom the spies saw at Hebron (Numbers 13:22). The giants who frightened ten of the spies are driven out by the one who was not afraid.

  • v18 "she urged him" — Achsah asks through her husband, then speaks for herself. What do you want? is mah lakh, what is to you.

  • v19 "Give me a blessing… springs of water" — berakhah, a gift; in the dry Negev the gift that matters is water.

  • v32 "twenty-nine cities" — the names listed in vv21–32 come to more than twenty-nine. Some may be double names for one place, or the count and the list may come from different times; the text is given as it stands.

  • v63 "could not drive out" — Jerusalem stays Jebusite until David takes it (2 Samuel 5:6–7).

chapters.title: "The Lot of Joseph: Ephraim"
chapters.html:
Joshua 16

The Sons of Joseph

1The lot for the sons of Joseph went out from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, into the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.

2It went out from Bethel to Luz and crossed to the border of the Archites at Ataroth,

3and went down westward to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, and it ended at the sea.

4So the sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.

Ephraim

5The border of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans was this: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon,

6and the border went out to the sea. Michmethath was on the north; the border turned east to Taanath-shiloh and passed along it east of Janoah,

7went down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, touched Jericho and ended at the Jordan.

8From Tappuah the border went west to the Brook of Kanah, and it ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans,

9together with the cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim within the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.

10But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day, and have become forced labor.

Notes

  • v1 "the lot for the sons of Joseph" — one lot for two tribes. Jacob had given Joseph a double share by adopting his sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, like Reuben and Simeon, shall be mine (Genesis 48:5). The complaint of 17:14 grows from this single lot.

  • v2 "from Bethel to Luz" — Genesis 28:19 says Luz was the name of the city at first, before Jacob called it Bethel. Here the two seem to be distinguished, perhaps the town and the nearby holy place.

  • vv5–8 Ephraim first — the younger son is placed before the elder, as Jacob crossed his hands in Genesis 48:14 and put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.

  • v9 "cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim within the inheritance of… Manasseh" — the two brother tribes' land is intertwined; 17:8–9 says the same from Manasseh's side.

  • v10 "they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer" — after Judah's failure at Jerusalem (15:63), Ephraim's at Gezer. 1 Kings 9:16 tells that Pharaoh later took Gezer, burned it with fire, and killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and gave it to his daughter, Solomon's wife. Forced labor, mas oved, is what Deuteronomy 20:10–15 allowed only for cities far away.

chapters.title: The Lot of Manasseh
chapters.html:
Joshua 17

Manasseh's Clans

1This was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn. To Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, Gilead and Bashan were given.

2The lot was also for the rest of the sons of Manasseh according to their clans: for the sons of Abiezer, the sons of Helek, the sons of Asriel, the sons of Shechem, the sons of Hepher and the sons of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, according to their clans.

The Daughters of Zelophehad

3Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters, and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

4They came before Eleazar the priest and before Joshua son of Nun and before the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So according to the command of the LORD he gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers.

5Ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan,

6because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.

Manasseh's Border

7The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which is east of Shechem; then the border went south to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.

8The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the sons of Ephraim.

9The border went down to the Brook of Kanah, south of the brook. These cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh was on the north side of the brook, and it ended at the sea.

10The land to the south was Ephraim's and to the north Manasseh's, and the sea was its border. They reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

11In Issachar and in Asher, Manasseh had Beth-shean and its towns, Ibleam and its towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, the inhabitants of En-dor and its towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns: the three heights.

12But the sons of Manasseh could not take possession of these cities, for the Canaanites were determined to live in that land.

13When the sons of Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but did not drive them out completely.

A Hill Country Covered in Forest

14The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, "Why have you given me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance, when I am a numerous people, since the LORD has blessed me so far?"

15Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear ground there for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

16The sons of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have chariots of iron, both those in Beth-shean and its towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."

17Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and have great strength. You shall not have only one lot.

18The hill country shall be yours. Though it is a forest, you shall clear it, and its farthest reaches shall be yours. For you shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong."

Notes

  • v1 "Machir… because he was a man of war" — Machir's line took Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan (13:31; Numbers 32:39–40). The west-bank clans follow in v2.

  • v2 "Abiezer" — the clan called Iezer in Numbers 26:30, of Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites. Gideon will come from Abiezer (Judges 6:11).

  • vv3–6 the daughters of Zelophehad — the five named in Numbers 27:1, who asked for their father's inheritance and received God's answer: The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say (Numbers 27:7). They come to Eleazar and Joshua to claim what Moses promised, and they receive it.

  • v5 "Ten portions" — five for the five brother clans, and five for Hepher's line through the five daughters; the text does not spell out the count.

  • v6 "the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons" — daughters counted as heirs beside sons.

  • v11 "the three heights" — sheloshet ha-nafet, obscure. It may refer to three of the towns on hills, perhaps Dor, on the heights of Dor (11:2).

  • vv12–13 "could not… did not drive them out completely" — horesh lo horisho, the verb doubled. As with Judah (15:63) and Ephraim (16:10), the Canaanites stay, now as forced labor.

  • vv14–18 "one lot and one portion" — the sons of Joseph complain that the single lot of 16:1 is too small. Joshua, himself of Ephraim (Numbers 13:8, Hoshea son of Nun for the tribe of Ephraim), gives them no more land but a task: clear the forest and drive out the Canaanites.

  • vv16, 18 "chariots of iron" — iron-fitted chariots on the plains of Beth-shean and Jezreel. Joshua answers the fear with a promise: you shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron.

chapters.title: Shiloh, and the Lot of Benjamin
chapters.html:
Joshua 18

The Tent of Meeting at Shiloh

1The whole congregation of the sons of Israel assembled at Shiloh, and they set up the tent of meeting there. The land was subdued before them.

2There remained among the sons of Israel seven tribes whose inheritance had not yet been divided.

3Joshua said to the sons of Israel, "How long will you be slack about going in to possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?

4Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They shall get up and walk through the land and write a description of it according to their inheritance, and come back to me.

5They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall stay in its territory on the south, and the house of Joseph shall stay in its territory on the north.

6You shall write a description of the land in seven portions and bring it here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

7For the Levites have no portion among you, for the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."

8So the men got up and went, and Joshua commanded those who went to write a description of the land, saying, "Go and walk through the land and write a description of it, and come back to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh."

9The men went and passed through the land and wrote a description of it by cities, in seven portions, in a book, and came to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.

10Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land to the sons of Israel according to their divisions.

Benjamin

11The lot of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin came up according to their clans, and the territory of their lot went out between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.

12Their border on the north side was from the Jordan; the border went up to the slope north of Jericho, went up through the hill country westward, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-aven.

13From there the border crossed to Luz, to the slope of Luz southward, that is, Bethel, and the border went down to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

14The border was drawn and turned on the west side southward from the mountain that faces Beth-horon on the south, and it ended at Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, a city of the sons of Judah. This was the west side.

15The south side was from the edge of Kiriath-jearim, and the border went out westward and went out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

16The border went down to the edge of the mountain that faces the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, which is at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom, to the slope of the Jebusite on the south, and went down to En-rogel.

17It was drawn on the north, went out to En-shemesh, went out to Geliloth, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

18It crossed to the slope opposite the Arabah on the north and went down to the Arabah.

19The border crossed to the slope of Beth-hoglah on the north, and the border ended at the north tongue of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the south border.

20The Jordan was its border on the east side. This is the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, by its borders all around, according to their clans.

21The cities of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin according to their clans were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,

22Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,

23Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,

24Chephar-haammonah, Ophni and Geba: twelve cities with their villages;

25Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

26Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,

27Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

28Zela, Haeleph, the Jebusite, that is, Jerusalem, Gibeath and Kiriath: fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin according to their clans.

Notes

  • v1 "Shiloh… the tent of meeting" — the center of worship moves from Gilgal to Shiloh, where it stays until the days of Eli and Samuel (1 Samuel 1:3). The land was subdued before them, nikhbeshah, the verb of Numbers 32:22, the land is subdued before the LORD.

  • v3 "How long will you be slack" — mitrappim, letting your hands drop. Seven tribes have not taken their share, and Joshua rebukes them.

  • vv4–9 the survey — three men from each tribe walk the land and write a description of it… in a book, al sefer. The land is divided by writing and by lot, before the LORD.

  • v7 "the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance" — a third way of saying it, after the offerings by fire (13:14) and the LORD Himself (13:33).

  • v11 "between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph" — Benjamin, Rachel's younger son, lies between the two great houses; Jerusalem sits on his border with Judah (v16, 15:8).

  • vv15–19 the south border — the same line as Judah's north border in 15:5–9, walked in the other direction.

  • v28 "the Jebusite, that is, Jerusalem" — listed among Benjamin's cities, though 15:63 says Judah could not drive the Jebusites out; Judges 1:21 says the same of Benjamin.

chapters.title: The Lots of the Remaining Tribes
chapters.html:
Joshua 19

Simeon

1The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the sons of Simeon according to their clans, and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the sons of Judah.

2They had for their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,

3Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,

4Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,

5Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,

6Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen cities with their villages;

7Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four cities with their villages;

8and all the villages around these cities as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Simeon according to their clans.

9The inheritance of the sons of Simeon was part of the portion of the sons of Judah, because the share of the sons of Judah was too large for them, so the sons of Simeon received an inheritance within their inheritance.

Zebulun

10The third lot came up for the sons of Zebulun according to their clans. The border of their inheritance reached to Sarid.

11Their border went up westward to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and touched the brook that is east of Jokneam.

12From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth-tabor, went out to Daberath and went up to Japhia.

13From there it crossed east toward the sunrise to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, went out to Rimmon and turned toward Neah.

14The border went around it on the north to Hannathon, and it ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el,

15with Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.

16This is the inheritance of the sons of Zebulun according to their clans, these cities with their villages.

Issachar

17The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the sons of Issachar according to their clans.

18Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,

19Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,

20Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,

21Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah and Beth-pazzez.

22The border touched Tabor, Shahazimah and Beth-shemesh, and their border ended at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.

23This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Issachar according to their clans, the cities with their villages.

Asher

24The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Asher according to their clans.

25Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,

26Allammelech, Amad and Mishal. It touched Carmel on the west and Shihor-libnath.

27It turned toward the sunrise to Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el northward, Beth-emek and Neiel, and went out to Cabul on the left,

28and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.

29The border turned to Ramah and to the fortified city of Tyre, and the border turned to Hosah, and it ended at the sea, from the region of Achzib,

30with Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages.

31This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Asher according to their clans, these cities with their villages.

Naphtali

32The sixth lot came out for the sons of Naphtali, for the sons of Naphtali according to their clans.

33Their border was from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum, and it ended at the Jordan.

34The border turned westward to Aznoth-tabor and went out from there to Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, touched Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise.

35The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,

36Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,

37Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor,

38Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities with their villages.

39This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali according to their clans, the cities with their villages.

Dan

40The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans.

41The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,

42Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,

43Elon, Timnah, Ekron,

44Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,

45Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon,

46Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory opposite Joppa.

47When the territory of the sons of Dan was lost to them, the sons of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, took it, struck it with the sword, possessed it and settled in it, and they called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

48This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans, these cities with their villages.

Joshua's Inheritance

49When they had finished distributing the land by its borders, the sons of Israel gave an inheritance among them to Joshua son of Nun.

50At the command of the LORD they gave him the city that he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and he built the city and settled in it.

51These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the sons of Israel distributed by lot in Shiloh before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.

Notes

  • vv1, 9 Simeon within Judah — Simeon gets no territory of its own, only cities inside Judah's. Jacob had said of Simeon and Levi, I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel (Genesis 49:7). Several of Simeon's cities appear in Judah's list in 15:26–32.

  • v2 "Beersheba, Sheba" — the count in v6 is thirteen, so Sheba may be a repetition of the second half of Beersheba; 1 Chronicles 4:28 lists Beersheba, Moladah without it.

  • vv10–16 Zebulun — inland in this list, though Jacob's blessing put Zebulun at the shore of the seas (Genesis 49:13).

  • v13 "Gath-hepher" — the hometown of Jonah son of Amittai (2 Kings 14:25).

  • v15 "Bethlehem" — a northern Bethlehem in Zebulun, not the Bethlehem of Judah.

  • v18 "Shunem" — where the Philistines camped before Saul's last battle (1 Samuel 28:4), and the home of the woman who sheltered Elisha (2 Kings 4:8).

  • v28 "as far as Great Sidon" — Asher's lot reaches the Phoenician coast, land Israel did not hold (Judges 1:31).

  • v47 "When the territory of the sons of Dan was lost to them" — Dan could not hold its lot by the coast and moved to the far north, to Leshem, called Laish in Judges 18:29, where the story is told at length.

  • vv49–50 Joshua last — the leader takes his own inheritance only after all the tribes have theirs, and asks for a town in the hill country of his own tribe, Ephraim. Judges 2:9 calls it Timnath-heres, the letters of serah reversed.

  • v51 — the division that began at Gilgal (14:1) ends at Shiloh, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

chapters.title: Towns of Refuge
chapters.html:
Joshua 20

Appoint the Towns of Refuge

1The LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'Appoint for yourselves the towns of refuge, of which I spoke to you through Moses,

3so that anyone who kills a person by mistake, unintentionally, may flee there. They shall be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

4He shall flee to one of these towns and stand at the entrance of the city gate and state his case in the hearing of the elders of that town. They shall take him into the town and give him a place, and he shall live with them.

5If the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not give up the one who killed into his hand, because he struck his neighbor unintentionally and had not hated him before.

6He shall live in that town until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest who is in office in those days. Then the one who killed may return and come to his own town and his own house, to the town from which he fled.'"

The Six Towns

7So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

8Beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they appointed Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

9These were the appointed towns for all the sons of Israel and for the guest who lives as a guest among them, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake may flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stands before the congregation.

Notes

  • v2 "of which I spoke to you through Moses" — the law of Numbers 35:9–34 and Deuteronomy 19:1–13, now carried out.

  • v3 "by mistake, unintentionally" — bi-shegagah, the word of Numbers 35:11, the one who kills a person by mistake, and bi-veli da'at, without knowing, the phrase of Deuteronomy 19:4.

  • v4 "at the entrance of the city gate" — the fugitive first pleads before the elders of the refuge town; the full trial comes later before the congregation (v6).

  • v5 "had not hated him before" — mi-temol shilshom, the test of Deuteronomy 19:4 and 4:42.

  • v6 "until the death of the high priest" — the rule of Numbers 35:25, until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil. The high priest's death closes the matter.

  • v7 "they set apart" — va-yaqdishu, made holy. The three western towns stand one in each region, north, center and south, so that none is too far away (Deuteronomy 19:3).

  • v8 Bezer, Ramoth, Golan — the three east of the Jordan that Moses had already named in Deuteronomy 4:43, Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau… Ramoth in Gilead… Golan in Bashan.

  • v9 "for the guest who lives as a guest among them" — refuge is not only for Israelites, as Numbers 35:15 said: for the guest and the resident among them.

chapters.title: The Towns of the Levites
chapters.html:
Joshua 21

The Levites Ask for Their Towns

1The heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua son of Nun and to the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the sons of Israel.

2They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given towns to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock."

3So the sons of Israel gave to the Levites from their inheritance, at the command of the LORD, these towns and their pasture lands.

The Lots of the Clans

4The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. To the sons of Aaron the priest, of the Levites, came thirteen towns by lot from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of the Simeonites and the tribe of Benjamin.

5The rest of the sons of Kohath received ten towns by lot from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

6The sons of Gershon received thirteen towns by lot from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

7The sons of Merari according to their clans received twelve towns from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and the tribe of Zebulun.

8The sons of Israel gave these towns and their pasture lands to the Levites by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.

The Sons of Aaron

9From the tribe of the sons of Judah and the tribe of the sons of Simeon they gave these towns, which are here mentioned by name.

10They went to the sons of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathites, of the sons of Levi, for the lot fell to them first.

11They gave them Kiriath-arba, Arba being the father of Anak, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with the pasture lands around it.

12But the fields of the town and its villages they had given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.

13To the sons of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, the town of refuge for the one who killed, with its pasture lands, Libnah with its pasture lands,

14Jattir with its pasture lands, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,

15Holon with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,

16Ain with its pasture lands, Juttah with its pasture lands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands: nine towns from these two tribes.

17From the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasture lands, Geba with its pasture lands,

18Anathoth with its pasture lands and Almon with its pasture lands: four towns.

19All the towns of the sons of Aaron, the priests: thirteen towns with their pasture lands.

The Rest of the Kohathites

20As for the clans of the sons of Kohath, the Levites who remained of the sons of Kohath, the towns of their lot were from the tribe of Ephraim.

21They gave them Shechem, the town of refuge for the one who killed, with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasture lands,

22Kibzaim with its pasture lands and Beth-horon with its pasture lands: four towns.

23From the tribe of Dan: Elteke with its pasture lands, Gibbethon with its pasture lands,

24Aijalon with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: four towns.

25From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: two towns.

26All the towns for the clans of the rest of the sons of Kohath: ten, with their pasture lands.

The Gershonites

27To the sons of Gershon, of the clans of the Levites, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, the town of refuge for the one who killed, with its pasture lands, and Beeshterah with its pasture lands: two towns.

28From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,

29Jarmuth with its pasture lands and En-gannim with its pasture lands: four towns.

30From the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,

31Helkath with its pasture lands and Rehob with its pasture lands: four towns.

32From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, the town of refuge for the one who killed, with its pasture lands, Hammoth-dor with its pasture lands and Kartan with its pasture lands: three towns.

33All the towns of the Gershonites according to their clans: thirteen towns with their pasture lands.

The Merarites

34To the clans of the sons of Merari, the rest of the Levites, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam with its pasture lands, Kartah with its pasture lands,

35Dimnah with its pasture lands and Nahalal with its pasture lands: four towns.

36From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasture lands, Jahaz with its pasture lands,

37Kedemoth with its pasture lands and Mephaath with its pasture lands: four towns.

38From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead, the town of refuge for the one who killed, with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,

39Heshbon with its pasture lands and Jazer with its pasture lands: four towns in all.

40All the towns for the sons of Merari according to their clans, the rest of the clans of the Levites: their lot was twelve towns.

41All the towns of the Levites within the holding of the sons of Israel were forty-eight towns with their pasture lands.

42These towns each had its pasture lands around it; so it was with all these towns.

Not One Word Failed

43So the LORD gave Israel all the land that He had sworn to give to their fathers, and they possessed it and settled in it.

44The LORD gave them rest all around, according to all that He had sworn to their fathers. Not one of all their enemies stood before them; the LORD gave all their enemies into their hand.

45Not one word failed of all the good word that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel. It all came to pass.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the Levites ask — as Caleb (14:6) and the daughters of Zelophehad (17:4) did, the Levites come and claim what Moses was commanded to give them (Numbers 35:2).

  • vv4–7 the three clans — Kohath, Gershon and Merari, the sons of Levi (Numbers 26:57). The priests, Aaron's sons, are a branch of Kohath and receive their towns in Judah, Simeon and Benjamin, near where the temple will stand.

  • v10 "the lot fell to them first" — Aaron's line is chosen first.

  • vv11–12 Hebron — the town goes to the priests, but the fields of the town and its villages stay Caleb's (14:13–14).

  • v18 "Anathoth" — the priestly town from which the prophet Jeremiah came (Jeremiah 1:1).

  • v25 "Gath-rimmon" — named also in v24, for Dan; 1 Chronicles 6:55 has Bileam in this second place. The repetition may be a copying slip.

  • vv13, 21, 27, 32, 38 the towns of refuge — all six are Levite towns, each marked the town of refuge for the one who killed: Hebron, Shechem, Golan, Kedesh, Ramoth, and Bezer (v36) without the phrase.

  • v41 "forty-eight towns" — the number of Numbers 35:7, All the towns that you give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns.

  • vv43–45 "Not one word failed" — lo nafal davar, not a word fell to the ground. The conquest summary ends in praise: It all came to pass. Joshua will say the same in 23:14, not one word has failed, and yet in 23:4–5 he speaks of these nations that remain: the promise is kept, and what remains is Israel's part. See the map after Joshua 24, stage 20.

chapters.title: The Altar by the Jordan
chapters.html:
Joshua 22

The Eastern Tribes Go Home

1Then Joshua called the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh,

2and said to them, "You have kept all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.

3You have not forsaken your brothers these many days, to this day, and you have kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God.

4Now the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, as He promised them. So now turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.

5Only be very careful to do the commandment and the instruction that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul."

6Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

7To the one half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a possession in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua had given a possession with their brothers beyond the Jordan to the west. When Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them,

8and said to them, "Go back to your tents with great wealth and with very much livestock, with silver and gold, with bronze and iron, and with very many clothes. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."

9So the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned, leaving the sons of Israel at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had taken possession of at the command of the LORD through Moses.

The Altar

10When they came to the region of the Jordan that is in the land of Canaan, the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look at.

11The sons of Israel heard it said, "The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar at the frontier of the land of Canaan, in the region of the Jordan, on the side belonging to the sons of Israel."

12When the sons of Israel heard it, the whole congregation of the sons of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go up against them to war.

13The sons of Israel sent to the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest,

14and ten leaders with him, one leader for each father's house from all the tribes of Israel, each of them the head of his father's house among the thousands of Israel.

15They came to the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, and spoke with them, saying,

16"A message from the whole congregation of the LORD: 'What is this breach of faith that you have committed against the God of Israel, turning away today from following the LORD by building yourselves an altar, to rebel today against the LORD?

17Is the guilt of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, though the plague came on the congregation of the LORD?

18You would turn away today from following the LORD! And it shall come to pass, if you rebel today against the LORD, that tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

19But if the land of your possession is unclean, cross over into the land of the LORD's possession, where the LORD's dwelling stands, and take your possession among us. Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.

20Did not Achan son of Zerah break faith over what was devoted to the LORD, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? He was not the only man who perished for his guilt.'"

The Answer of the Eastern Tribes

21Then the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and said to the heads of the thousands of Israel,

22"The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD! He knows, and let Israel itself know: if it was in rebellion or in breach of faith against the LORD, do not save us this day!

23If we have built ourselves an altar to turn away from following the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, or to make peace offerings on it, may the LORD Himself require it.

24No — we did it out of anxiety over a matter, thinking, 'Tomorrow your sons may say to our sons, "What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?

25The LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you, you sons of Reuben and sons of Gad. You have no portion in the LORD." So your sons may make our sons stop fearing the LORD.'

26So we said, 'Let us now build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,

27but to be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we do serve the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings and our sacrifices and our peace offerings, so that your sons do not say to our sons tomorrow, "You have no portion in the LORD."'

28We said, 'And it shall come to pass, if they say this to us or to our generations tomorrow, that we will say, "See the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but to be a witness between us and you."'

29Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering or for sacrifice, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands before His dwelling."

A Witness Between Us

30When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the sons of Manasseh spoke, it was good in their eyes.

31Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the sons of Manasseh, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against the LORD. Now you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the LORD."

32Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad, from the land of Gilead, to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and brought back word to them.

33The report was good in the eyes of the sons of Israel. The sons of Israel blessed God and spoke no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land where the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad lived.

34The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad called the altar Witness: "For it is a witness between us that the LORD is God."

Notes

  • vv1–6 the eastern tribes released — the promise of Numbers 32 and Joshua 1:12–18 kept. They have not forsaken their brothers, and Joshua sends them home with a blessing and a charge that repeats Deuteronomy's heart: to love the LORD your God… with all your heart and with all your soul.

  • v10 "a great altar to look at" — mizbeach gadol le-mar'eh, built to be seen. The whole quarrel turns on what it is for.

  • v16 "this breach of faith" — ma'al, the word used of Achan in 7:1. The western tribes suspect the easterners of a second Achan's sin, and v20 says so outright.

  • v17 "the guilt of Peor" — the worship of the Baal of Peor in Numbers 25, where those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand. Phinehas, who leads this embassy, is the priest who stopped that plague (Numbers 25:11).

  • v19 "if the land of your possession is unclean" — the offer is generous: if the east bank is not fit for worship, come and share the west.

  • v22 "The Mighty One, God, the LORD!" — El Elohim YHWH, three names of God, twice: the strongest oath the easterners can swear. He knows — the answer is put first to God, then to Israel.

  • v28 "See the pattern of the altar of the LORD" — tavnit, the word of Exodus 25:9, the pattern of the dwelling. The altar is a copy, a model of the real one at Shiloh, built to be looked at, not used.

  • v31 "Today we know that the LORD is among us" — the danger of chapter 7 is not repeated; the peace between the tribes is itself a sign of God's presence.

  • v34 "called the altar Witness" — Ed is not written in the Hebrew as the altar's name; the sentence reads called the altar: for it is a witness between us. Many translations supply the name Witness, as this one does, because the explanation that follows gives it.

So we said, 'Let us now build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,

but to be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we do serve the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings and our sacrifices and our peace offerings, so that your sons do not say to our sons tomorrow, "You have no portion in the LORD."'

We said, 'And it shall come to pass, if they say this to us or to our generations tomorrow, that we will say, "See the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but to be a witness between us and you."'

Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering or for sacrifice, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands before His dwelling."
A Witness Between Us

When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the sons of Manasseh spoke, it was good in their eyes.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the sons of Manasseh, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against the LORD. Now you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the LORD."

Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad, from the land of Gilead, to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and brought back word to them.

The report was good in the eyes of the sons of Israel. The sons of Israel blessed God and spoke no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land where the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad lived.
The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad called the altar Witness: "For it is a witness between us that the LORD is God."

chapters.title: Joshua's Farewell to the Leaders
chapters.html:
Joshua 23

The LORD Fought for You

1A long time afterward, when the LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and Joshua was old, coming on in days,

2Joshua called for all Israel, for their elders and their heads, their judges and their officials, and said to them, "I am old, coming on in days.

3You have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, for it is the LORD your God who has fought for you.

4See, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes these nations that remain, along with all the nations I have cut off, from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.

5The LORD your God will push them back before you and drive them out of your sight, and you shall possess their land, as the LORD your God promised you.

Hold Fast to the LORD

6Be very strong, then, to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the instruction of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right or to the left,

7so that you do not mix with these nations that remain among you. Do not speak the names of their gods, do not swear by them, do not serve them and do not bow down to them.

8Hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.

9The LORD has driven out great and strong nations before you, and as for you, no one has stood against you to this day.

10One man of you chases a thousand, for it is the LORD your God who fights for you, as He promised you.

11Take great care for your own lives to love the LORD your God.

12For if you ever turn back and cling to what is left of these nations that remain among you, and marry among them, and you go in to them and they to you,

13know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive these nations out before you. They will be a trap and a snare for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.

Not One Word Has Failed

14Today I am going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and with all your soul that not one word has failed of all the good words that the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All have come to pass for you; not one word of them has failed.

15And it shall come to pass that just as every good word the LORD your God spoke to you has come upon you, so the LORD will bring upon you every evil word, until He has destroyed you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you,

16when you break the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will perish quickly from the good land that He has given you."

Notes

  • v1 "old, coming on in days" — zaqen ba ba-yamim, the words said of Joshua in 13:1 and of Abraham in Genesis 24:1. The chapter is Joshua's farewell, as Deuteronomy is Moses'.

  • v3 "it is the LORD your God who has fought for you" — the promise of Deuteronomy 1:30 and 3:22, the LORD your God is the one who fights for you. Joshua repeats it in v10.

  • v6 "not turning aside from it to the right or to the left" — the charge given to Joshua himself in 1:7, now passed on to the people.

  • v7 "Do not speak the names of their gods" — lo tazkiru, do not call to mind, do not mention, as in Exodus 23:13, The name of other gods you shall not mention; it shall not be heard on your mouth.

  • v8 "Hold fast" — tidbaqu, the verb of Deuteronomy 10:20 and 13:4. In v12 the same verb turns the other way: cling to the nations that remain.

  • v10 "One man of you chases a thousand" — the reverse of the curse in Deuteronomy 32:30, How could one chase a thousand… unless their Rock had sold them?

  • v12 "if you ever turn back" — shov tashuvu, turn back, you turn back, a doubled verb for emphasis. So in v13, yadoa ted'u, know, you will know: know for certain.

  • v13 "a trap and a snare… a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes" — the warning of Numbers 33:55, barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, with the thorns moved to the eyes. Judges 2:3 recalls it when the warning comes true.

  • v14 "the way of all the earth" — death. David says the same words to Solomon in 1 Kings 2:2. Not one word has failed repeats 21:45.

  • vv15–16 — the good words and the evil words are both the LORD's; the blessing and the curse of Deuteronomy 28 stand side by side.

chapters.title: The Covenant at Shechem
chapters.html:
Joshua 24

What the LORD Has Done

1Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem and called for the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges and its officials, and they presented themselves before God.

2Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your fathers lived beyond the River — Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor — and they served other gods.

3I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan. I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac,

4and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.

5I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought you out.

6I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea, and the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.

7They cried out to the LORD, and He put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness a long time.

8I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand. You took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.

9Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam son of Beor to curse you,

10but I would not listen to Balaam. He blessed you instead, and I delivered you out of his hand.

11You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho, and the lords of Jericho fought against you — the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite and the Jebusite — and I gave them into your hand.

12I sent the hornet before you, and it drove them out before you, the two kings of the Amorites — not by your sword and not by your bow.

13I gave you a land you had not labored for, and cities you had not built, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.'

Choose Today

14"And now fear the LORD and serve Him in wholeness and in truth. Put away the gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

15But if it seems wrong in your eyes to serve the LORD, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: whether the gods your fathers served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

16The people answered, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!

17For it is the LORD our God who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, who did these great signs before our eyes, and kept us on all the way we went and among all the peoples through whom we passed.

18The LORD drove out before us all the peoples, and the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, for He is our God."

19Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD, for He is a holy God. He is a jealous God; He will not forgive your transgressions or your sins.

20If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and do you harm and consume you, after having done you good."

21The people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."

22Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve Him." They said, "We are witnesses."

23"And now put away the foreign gods that are among you, and turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."

24The people said to Joshua, "The LORD our God we will serve, and His voice we will obey."

The Stone of Witness

25So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set for them a statute and a rule at Shechem.

26Joshua wrote these words in the book of the instruction of God. He took a great stone and set it up there under the terebinth that was in the sanctuary of the LORD.

27Joshua said to all the people, "This stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It shall be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God."

28Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.

Three Burials

29And it came to pass after these things that Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, a hundred and ten years old.

30They buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

31Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and had known all the work the LORD did for Israel.

32The bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred qesitah. It became an inheritance of the sons of Joseph.

33Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given him in the hill country of Ephraim.

Notes

  • v1 "to Shechem" — where Abram first built an altar in the land (Genesis 12:6–7) and where the blessing and curse were read at Mount Ebal (8:30–35). The Greek has to Shiloh, here and in v25, where it adds before the tent of the God of Israel.

  • v2 "beyond the River… they served other gods" — the River is the Euphrates. Terah's household is the start of the story (Genesis 11:31), and Joshua does not hide that it began in idolatry.

  • v7 "He put darkness between you and the Egyptians" — ma'afel, found only here; the event is Exodus 14:20, cloud and darkness. The speech moves from I to He and back: Joshua is speaking the LORD's words.

  • v10 "He blessed you instead" — va-yevarekh barokh, a doubled verb, he blessed, blessing. Deuteronomy 23:5 tells the same story: the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you.

  • v12 "the hornet… the two kings of the Amorites" — the hornet of Exodus 23:28 and Deuteronomy 7:20; the two kings are Sihon and Og, east of the Jordan. The Greek has twelve kings of the Amorites.

  • v14 "in wholeness and in truth" — be-tamim u-ve-emet. Tamim of a person is wholeness toward God, as in Deuteronomy 18:13, You shall be whole with the LORD your God.

  • v15 "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD" — the choice is put to the people, but Joshua has already made his.

  • v19 "You cannot serve the LORD, for He is a holy God" — Elohim qedoshim hu, with the adjective in the plural to match Elohim. Joshua's refusal is meant to make the people's yes a considered one. A jealous God is El qanno, a form of the El qanna of Exodus 20:5.

  • vv26–27 "a great stone… a witness against us" — as the altar by the Jordan was a witness in 22:34. The terebinth recalls Genesis 35:4, where Jacob hid the foreign gods under the terebinth that is by Shechem; here too the people are told to put away foreign gods (v23, Genesis 35:2).

  • vv29–33 three burials — Joshua, Joseph and Eleazar. Joseph's bones, carried out of Egypt at his own request (Genesis 50:25, Exodus 13:19), are laid in the field Jacob bought (Genesis 33:19). The Greek adds that the flint knives of the circumcision at Gilgal (5:2) were buried with Joshua, and after v33 it adds that Phinehas served as priest after Eleazar, and that Israel then served Astarte and was given into the hand of Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years — the story Judges 3 tells. See the map after Joshua 24, stage 21.

<script>
(function(){
  var R = document.getElementById('jm');

    $('.jm-scale span').textContent = m + ' miles';
  }
  // the camera for stage i: the whole map if chosen, else the stage's own frame, else its view
  function target(i){
    var s = D.stages[i];
    return chosen === 'j' ? 'j' : s.v ? 's' + i : (chosen || s.c);
  }
  function setCam(c, anim){
    if (c === cam) return Promise.resolve();
    cam = c;
    svg.classList.remove('zoomed');
    $$('.jm-view button').forEach(function(b){ b.classList.toggle('on', b.getAttribute('data-cam') === (c === 'j' ? 'j' : 'l')); });

    cancelAnimationFrame(raf);

    var t0 = performance.now();

    return new Promise(function(res){
      function step(now){

        layout();
        if (p < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(step); else res();
      }
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    });
  }
  function mask(g){ return svg.querySelector(g.getAttribute('mask').slice(4, -1) + ' .mk'); }

      var it = {m: mask(g), d: t, dur: Math.min(2600, Math.max(650, L * 5))};
      t += it.dur * .8;
      it.m.style.strokeDasharray = '1 1'; it.m.style.strokeDashoffset = '1';
      return it;
    });

    return new Promise(function(res){

        var done = true;

    if (playing){ stop(); return; }

  }
  function step(to){ stop(); go(to, true).then(function(){ setPlay(false); }); }

  }

  }
  function placeInfo(id){

    });

      (stages.length ? '<p>' + stages.map(function(j){ return '<a href="#" data-goto="' + j + '">' + (j + 1) + '. ' + esc(D.stages[j].t) + '</a>'; }).join('<br>') + '</p>' : ''));
  }

  // --- zooming in and out, and dragging the map ---

  }

  });

      svg.classList.add('drag'); svg.setPointerCapture(drag.id);

    vb = [drag.vb[0] - dx * drag.k, drag.vb[1] - dy * drag.k, vb[2], vb[3]];

  });

  svg.addEventListener('pointerup', endDrag);

    var pageH = Math.floor(innerWidth * 8.4 / 6.2), map1 = $('.jm-map');
    var bottom = function(e){ return e.getBoundingClientRect().bottom + scrollY; };
    holder.style.marginTop = '0';
    if (bottom(map1) + 10 + holder.getBoundingClientRect().height + 10 <= pageH){
      // two landscape maps share a page
      map1.style.marginBottom = '10px';
      holder.style.marginBottom = Math.max(10, pageH - bottom(holder)) + 'px';
    } else {
      map1.style.marginBottom = Math.max(10, pageH - bottom(map1)) + 'px';
      holder.style.marginBottom = Math.max(10, 2 * pageH - bottom(holder)) + 'px';
    }
  }
})();
</script>
</div>
